evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline accuracy is measured on held-out test splits with independent answering models and external LLM judges, with 97.3% agreement between GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B judges.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out test question-answering accuracy judged by GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B over answers from Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and GPT-4o-mini.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: LightGBM LambdaRank trained on gold turn annotations from the 152 development questions, or distilled from Qwen3-8B offline scores.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that AgentMemRec outperforms turn-level context selectors and LLM-built memories by 10 to 33 points while matching a 64-call LLM reranker at 3.2x lower latency and cost are supported by comprehensive tables, calibrations across GPT-4o and Qwen judges, and error/filler analyses.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations are rigorous across LongMemEval-S, LongMemEval-M, and LoCoMo, accounting for inference non-determinism via multi-budget decoding, paired bootstrap statistical tests, and explicit factorizations separating candidate recall, ranking completeness, and complete slate rewards.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline QA accuracy is validated on held-out test instances with independent answering models and external LLM judges, showing strong agreement (97.3% between GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B judges) across multiple decodes.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: End-to-end downstream question-answering accuracy evaluated on held-out test splits using GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B judges across answer generations from Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and GPT-4o-mini.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: LightGBM LambdaRank trained on pairwise gold turn annotations from the 152 development questions (or distilled from Qwen3-8B offline scores).

primary.limitations: The authors identify degradation on instances requiring evidence across three or more sessions (kappa >= 3), sensitivity to near-miss filler distractors in complete slates, and performance variations across target answering models.
primary.method_assessment: The method is clearly specified: a 128-candidate pool formed from BM25 and bge-m3 dense embeddings via reciprocal rank fusion, scored with a 10-feature LightGBM LambdaRank model trained on development split gold annotations, followed by greedy budget filling without per-query cutoffs.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a sound theoretical formulation uniting memory architectures into a recommender cascade and demonstrates strong empirical gains using zero-LLM-call ranking, supported by thorough baseline reproductions, cost measurements, and independent evaluation controls.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formalizes long-term LLM agent memory selection as budgeted slate recommendation and presents AgentMemRec, a non-LLM cascade using reciprocal rank fusion over lexical/dense channels, LightGBM LambdaRank over ten inexpensive features, and budget filling.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a sound theoretical formulation uniting memory architectures into a recommender cascade and demonstrates strong empirical gains using zero-LLM-call ranking, supported by thorough baseline reproductions, cost measurements, and independent evaluation controls.

blocking_reasons: The LLM-judge used for headline outcomes is also used as an LLM backbone in the evaluated systems, so the reported gains are not shown to be independent of the evaluation signal.
The evaluator-independent F1 measurements do not consistently corroborate the headline LLM-judge improvements; in several settings F1 decreases or remains mixed relative to baselines.
The paper does not report evaluator calibration, inter-rater agreement against independent labels, or a separately calibrated judge, leaving independence of the headline metric unestablished.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Token-level F1 scores are reported alongside the LLM-judge metric, but they move inconsistently with the headline LLM-judge gains, with MaC not clearly best on several F1 dimensions.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline accuracy is established by an LLM judge, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, over the benchmark question sets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No training or tuning against the judge is reported; construction, planning, and answer generation rely on prompt-guided LLM inference with heuristic repair routines.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported gains (up to 15.91% higher LLM-judge accuracy on LOCOMO and 9.06% on LONGMEMEVAL, with substantial token reductions) are directly corroborated by empirical results in Tables 1-4 and ablation studies.
primary.evaluation_assessment: MaC is systematically evaluated on LOCOMO and LONGMEMEVAL across three backbone models, measuring both standard F1 and LLM-Judge accuracy against four recent baselines, supplemented by comprehensive token consumption, latency, storage, and ablation analyses.
